To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) there is a wide variety of ongoing clinical trials addressing COVID 19, 2) most of the trials are not registered, 3) most of them are interventional studies and the majority of them are randomized controlled trials, 4) the majority of trials are in China and the most studied intervention is hydroxychloroquine, 5) there are ongoing trials evaluating a wide variety of interventions and there is not a single trial evaluating a vaccine.

the clinical trials registered in the databases address the evaluation of different therapeutic options, including antiviral drugs (remdesivir, lopinavir-ritonavir, interferon-β1b), immunomodulatory agents (tocilizumab) and convalescent plasma, as well as the use of corticosteroids, and that there are no studies evaluating the use of antibiotics or antimalarials in patients with COVID 19.
there is a lack of randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and a high number of non-randomized studies (NRCTs) with low quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1.
the development of new diagnostic methods and therapeutic strategies against COVID 19.

the evaluation of the following therapeutic options: antivirals (lopinavir/ritonavir, favipiravir, interferon beta, remdesivir, chloroquine/hydroxychloroquine); immunomodulators (tocilizumab, anakinra); and convalescent plasma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is not yet conclusive for any therapeutic intervention for COVID 19, and there are many ongoing trials that will provide more information on the efficacy of these therapies.
there is no evidence of benefit from any of the treatments that have been evaluated in clinical trials.
there is insufficient data to support or refute any of the proposed interventions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
most of the clinical trials registered so far are for therapeutic options and not for diagnostic or preventive measures.
the majority of the trials have been registered in China and are focused on evaluating antivirals, convalescent plasma and immunotherapy.
the majority of these studies are not yet recruiting participants, and many of them are not yet published.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of studies are evaluating drugs that are already in clinical use.
there are many ongoing studies evaluating a variety of therapeutic options for COVID 19.
most studies are evaluating the efficacy of antiviral agents and/or immune modulating drugs.
